fields.headline: No Voters Deleted; Records in Two Carrow Precincts Being Corrected
fields.subhead: Affected voters can vote a provisional ballot; Polling Location 6 has not moved
fields.body: No voters were deleted. 1,186 records in two Carrow precincts were wrongly marked as mail ballot issued after an employee account was misused overnight. We are correcting them. Any voter shown as mail ballot issued can vote a provisional ballot at the Early Vote Center or on Election Day, and it will be counted once the record is verified. Polling Location 6 has not moved: it is at Carrow Community Church, 77 West Fourth Street.

snapshot.title: Press Release: Voter Registration Data Restored After Cyber Incident

fields.headline: Voter Registration Data Restored; 1,186 Records Corrected After Unauthorized Access
fields.subhead: All voters in Precincts 111 and 112 are eligible to vote in person. No one was deleted from the system.
fields.body:
The Lisle County Board of Elections has confirmed that unauthorized access to the county voter registration system, VoterTrack, resulted in 1,186 records being falsely marked as having received mail ballots. The incident was detected and contained by 09:30. No voter records were deleted, and all voters who appear in the system are eligible to vote in person.

The Board has restored the correct data using a trusted, air-gapped export from October 28, 2026. The results website, hotline, and public information channels have been updated to reflect verified information. The Board is working with CISA and the Ohio Secretary of State to investigate the breach.

All voters are advised to verify their registration status at lislevotes.example/voter-verification. The Board urges the public not to share unverified claims or rumors. For more information, visit the official website or call the hotline at (877) 876-2455.

The Board reaffirms that every eligible voter in Lisle County will be able to cast a ballot on Election Day.
